en.title: Ryan Reynolds & Hugh Jackman Reportedly Earn Writing Credits on Avengers: Doomsday
en.summary: The MCU's next major team-up film might have a few more familiar names in its writing credits. Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman are rumored to be recognized by the WGA for their contributions to the upcoming blockbuster.
en.body:
The Writers Guild of America (WGA) has a reputation for meticulously tracking writing credits, and it seems even the biggest Marvel Cinematic Universe projects are subject to its scrutiny. Recent whispers suggest that **Ryan Reynolds** and **Hugh Jackman**, the beloved on-screen duo poised to bring **Deadpool** and **Wolverine** into the MCU fold in **Avengers: Doomsday**, may be receiving official writing credit for the film.

While Marvel Studios has been characteristically coy about the specifics of their narrative integration, the actors' involvement has been heavily teased. Reynolds' surprise appearance at San Diego Comic-Con in a Deadpool costume and Jackman's video confirmation at D23 have only fueled speculation. Now, the potential for writing credit, reportedly as part of the "Additional Literary Material" category, adds another layer to their anticipated roles. This wouldn't be the first time Reynolds has been involved in the writing process, as he co-wrote **Deadpool 2** and **Deadpool & Wolverine**. The WGA's decision, if confirmed, acknowledges that the actors' unique comedic sensibilities and improvisational contributions have significantly shaped the film's script, moving beyond mere on-set ad-libs to tangible narrative input.

## A Surprise for Screenwriting Standards

The inclusion of actors in writing credits, particularly for a project of **Avengers: Doomsday**'s magnitude, is a significant point of interest for fans and industry observers alike. It speaks to a modern approach in blockbuster filmmaking where lead actors, especially those deeply associated with their characters like Reynolds, often have a profound impact on the script's development. The WGA's guidelines are notoriously complex, and earning a credit typically requires a substantial contribution. This rumored recognition highlights the unique creative synergy between Reynolds, Jackman, and the film's core writing team, which includes established MCU scribes like **Michael Waldron** and **Stephen McFeely**. It suggests that the dynamic, often chaotic energy of Deadpool and the gravitas of Wolverine have been woven into the very fabric of the script, not just layered on top during filming.

## What This Means for Fans

For the passionate fanbase eagerly awaiting the integration of these iconic characters into the main MCU narrative, this news is a fascinating peek behind the curtain. It suggests that the humor and meta-commentary fans expect from **Deadpool** and the raw intensity of **Wolverine** will be authentically represented, thanks to the actors' direct influence on the writing. The WGA credit implies that the spirit of Reynolds' and Jackman's off-screen chemistry has translated directly into the film's dialogue and plot. This level of actor involvement can often lead to more organic and resonant character portrayals, which is precisely what fans are hoping for as these beloved figures make their grand entrance into the Avengers saga. The stakes are high for **Avengers: Doomsday** to deliver a satisfying convergence of multiple storylines and characters, and this reported writing credit suggests a collaborative effort to ensure that the fan-favorite elements are front and center.

## What's Next

While the WGA has not yet officially confirmed these credits, details surrounding **Avengers: Doomsday** are expected to continue unfolding. The film is slated for release in May 2026, and further announcements regarding its creative team and narrative direction are anticipated as production progresses.

content_raw: Look, nobody really believes Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds won’t be reprising their roles as Wolverine and Deadpool in next month’s Avengers: Doomsday . Marvel Studios hasn’t exactly been subtle about their inclusion: Reynolds showed up at July’s San Diego Comic-Con in a gray ‘Pool outfit and asked Kevin Feige if he could be in the superhero smash-em-up; Jackman appeared via video during Disney’s D23 presentation in August and tacitly confirmed his participation in the film. So, when we see Deadpool scratching his tush in New Avengers Tower in December, nobody should be falling out of their theater seats in surprise. However, the Writers Guild of America does have a surprise in store ( per Gizmodo ), at least for those more concerned with screenwriter credits than with surprise superhero appearances. If you click over to the WGA page for Avengers: Doomsday , you may notice Jackman and Reynolds’ names among the many, many writers listed in the film’s Additional Literary Material credits. The duo, known for their ad-libbing monkeyshines in Deadpool & Wolverine , join Stephen McFeely and Michael Waldron (the film’s main credited screenwriters), Eric Pearson ( The Fantastic Four: First Steps , Thunderbolts* ), Chris McKenna ( Avengers: Infinity War , Avengers: Endgame ), Erik Sommers ( Spider-Man: Homecoming ), Jeff Loveness ( Ant-Man And The Wasp: Quantumania ), Andrew Lanham ( Shang-Chi And The Legend Of The Ten Rings ), and Destin Daniel Cretton ( Shang-Chi , Spider-Man: Brand New Day ). Why? How? Huh? All valid questions. Even if much of the actors’ contributions to the final screenplay amount to little more than improvisational berserker rages and/or ball-jokes, it’s clearly enough to warrant a WGA credit. (While Reynolds has previous writing credits for Deadpool 2 and Deadpool & Wolverine , it doesn’t appear Jackman has WGA membership–though we guess he soon will!) We’ll just have to wait until the December 18 release of Avengers: Doomsday to see whether Deadpool’s patented irreverence will disrupt the apparent severity of its multiverse-ending storyline, or whether the Merc With The Mouth will be put on a leash. (Not a real leash! This is still a Disney movie!) Update: Ryan Reynolds has just posted the film’s credits on his X account. — Ryan Reynolds (@VancityReynolds) November 12, 2026
